name: Ramp
text: Add a high-contrast focus ring that appears immediately on keyboard navigation. This enhances visibility for users who rely on keyboard navigation, ensuring they can easily identify which element is selected. While this may sacrifice some stylistic design for greater accessibility, the trade-off is worthwhile as it aligns with our commitment to making EXCAVA usable for everyone.

name: Reader
text: A high-contrast focus ring can create a visual "siren" effect, drawing too much attention and potentially distracting users rather than guiding them. A better alternative is a subtle focus ring that still provides adequate visibility without overwhelming the design. To settle the argument, usability testing with real users should be conducted to determine the effectiveness of both options in enhancing navigation without compromising the overall user experience.

name: Ramp
text:
We should implement a subtle focus ring that is visible to users who rely on keyboard navigation while respecting motion preferences. This approach enhances usability without overwhelming the design, striking a balance between accessibility and aesthetics. The trade-off is that it may not be as immediately noticeable as a high-contrast option, but it provides a less distracting user experience, which can be more beneficial in the long run.

name: Reader
text: The subtle focus ring still risks being insufficient for users with low vision who need *immediate* and *unmistakable* visual feedback. A better alternative is a toggleable high-contrast mode that users can activate—this respects individual needs without forcing a one-size-fits-all solution. Settle the argument with user testing: measure task completion time and subjective frustration for both focus ring styles with low-vision participants.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Ship a **subtle high-contrast focus indicator** with a **toggleable option** for users to select a stronger contrast if needed; this will enhance accessibility while respecting individual preferences. The design team owns this implementation.
